transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um, well... my manager said I needed to come see someone. It's because of work. I guess what really scared everyone there is that I started freezing up right in the middle of service. Or I'd start doing things completely out of order. Like, the other day I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks. 

Which, honestly, the soda station is always so sticky anyway. The Diet Coke syrup is constantly running out because people drink so much of it now. I remember when I was taking classes at the community college, my roommate would drink like four Diet Cokes a day just to get through midterms. She was a nursing major, so she was always super stressed out. We had this tiny mini-fridge in our place that was basically just full of those silver cans, and she'd stack all the empties on the windowsill to see how high they could go before they fell over. I think she ended up moving to Florida or something...
When you start talking, do people often tell you that your thoughts are hard to follow or that you go off on tangents?

Um, no, not really? I haven't noticed anyone saying that to me. They usually just tell me to hurry up. Like my manager, he's always just pointing at the ticket printer and telling me to move. 

That machine has the most annoying beep, actually. It's this sharp, high-pitched screech every time an order comes through. My dog used to make a noise exactly like that when she wanted to go outside. She was a beagle mix, and they are just so loud. We ended up putting a little bell by the back door for her to ring, but she figured out pretty fast that if she rang it, we'd give her a treat when she came back inside. So she just started batting at it all day long, even if she didn't have to go to the bathroom. Dogs are just so smart about food, you know?
Have you been hearing voices or other sounds that other people don’t seem to hear?

Um, well... yeah, sometimes. Like, when I'm closing up the restaurant, or even when I'm just at home in my own kitchen, I'll hear this woman's voice. She'll say my name, or she'll tell me I'm doing the till count wrong. It's so clear that I actually answer her out loud before I realize nobody else is there. 

Which is embarrassing, honestly, because I'm usually pretty good at counting. I used to help my mom balance her checkbook when I was in middle school. She had this really nice leather checkbook cover that had a little calculator built into the flap. It was one of those solar-powered ones, so you had to hold it right under the kitchen light to get it to turn on. We had this awful fluorescent light in the kitchen that would buzz all the time. My dad said he was going to fix the ballast in it, but he never got around to it before they sold the house. They moved to Arizona because my mom's arthritis was getting bad in the cold weather, and she heard the dry heat is supposed to be really good for your joints. I think she started taking water aerobics classes out there...
Have you had a period lately where you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Um, no, not really. I usually feel pretty exhausted after my shifts, honestly. Being on my feet all day just drains me, so I try to sleep as much as I can when I get home. 

I bought this really nice mattress topper last year to help with my back pain from standing so much. It's one of those memory foam ones infused with cooling gel. The guy at the store said it was the same technology they use in astronaut suits, which I thought was kind of weird. Like, why would an astronaut need a mattress? But I guess space is really cold, or maybe it's really hot depending on if you're facing the sun or not. I watched this documentary once about how they have to exercise on the International Space Station so their bones don't turn to mush. They have these special bungee cord treadmills. I tried getting a treadmill for my apartment once, but the people downstairs complained about the thumping noise. They were always complaining, though. The guy played the bass guitar at like two in the morning, so I don't know why he was so mad about my treadmill...
Before these experiences started, did you have any head injury, seizure, or other major medical illness?

Um, no, I've never had anything like that. No head injuries or seizures or anything. I've always been pretty healthy, honestly. 

Except for when I got my tonsils out when I was seven. That was a whole ordeal because I was supposed to get to eat all the ice cream I wanted, but my throat hurt so bad I couldn't even swallow the melted part. My grandma brought over this huge tub of Neapolitan, which is the worst flavor anyway because the strawberry always bleeds into the vanilla and it just tastes fake. She used to make her own ice cream in the summer with one of those old wooden crank machines. You had to put rock salt and ice around the canister, and my cousin and I would take turns cranking it until our arms felt like they were going to fall off. He ended up joining the Navy right out of high school and got stationed somewhere in Japan. He sent me a postcard once with a picture of a really beautiful temple on it, but the post office stamped right over the front of it so you could barely see the roof...
Have you had a period recently when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um, no, I wouldn't say depressed. I haven't been sad all day or anything like that. Mostly I just go to work and try to get through my shifts. 

Though there is this one hostess at the restaurant, Chloe, who is always crying in the breakroom lately. I think she's just really stressed out because she's planning her wedding. She showed me pictures of the centerpieces she wants, and they're these massive glass vases filled with water and floating candles. I told her that sounds like a total disaster waiting to happen with people reaching across the table for the breadbaskets. We serve these really good garlic knots at work, and they come with a side of marinara that the prep guy makes from scratch every morning. He uses these special imported tomatoes, which he insists are the only ones you should ever use for sauce. I tried growing tomatoes on my balcony once, but the squirrels kept taking exactly one bite out of the green ones and just leaving them sitting on the railing. It's so frustrating when animals do that. Like, if you're going to steal it, at least finish eating it, you know? My neighbor bought this plastic owl to try and scare them away, but the pigeons just ended up sitting right on its head...
About how long have you been hearing that woman’s voice?

Um, well, the really clear ones... like her voice, and when I started realizing that the people at work—the customers and the other servers—were actually targeting me... that's been going on for about four months now. 

It started right around the time they changed the uniform shirts at work. We used to wear these really breathable cotton polos, but corporate switched us to these stiff, synthetic button-downs that don't breathe at all. They get so staticky in the winter. I tried using those dryer sheets, the ones that smell like lavender, but then I read this article online about how the chemicals in dryer sheets coat your clothes and make them less absorbent. Which is a huge problem if you spill water on yourself during a shift, because instead of soaking in, it just rolls right off onto your shoes. I had to buy new non-slip shoes because my old ones got completely soaked and started smelling like mildew. I tried putting baking soda in them, but it just clumped up into these weird little rocks. Have you ever noticed how baking soda comes in that exact same orange box no matter what brand you buy? It's like there's a monopoly on baking soda packaging. My mom used to keep an open box in the back of the fridge, right next to the jar of pickles that no one ever ate...
Since these problems began, have they lasted for more than one month without going away?

Um, I'm not really sure. I haven't exactly been marking it on a calendar or anything to see if it stops for a whole month. It just kind of blends together, you know? 

Speaking of calendars, my manager at the restaurant, Rick, uses this giant dry-erase calendar in the back office for our schedules, but he refuses to buy the right markers. He always gets these cheap permanent ones by mistake, and then he has to scrub the board with rubbing alcohol every Sunday night to get the names off. The whole office ends up smelling exactly like a hospital. I really hate that smell. It reminds me of when I had to take my cat, Barnaby, to the vet because he swallowed a piece of yarn from my knitting basket. The vet said string is actually the most dangerous thing a cat can swallow because it gets all tangled up inside them like an accordion. The surgery cost me a fortune, which I had to put on my credit card. The interest rate on that card is absolutely ridiculous, it's like twenty-something percent. I keep meaning to transfer the balance to one of those zero-percent introductory offer cards you get in the mail, but they always print the terms and conditions in that tiny, tiny font that you practically need a magnifying glass to read...
Have these experiences been going on for six months or longer?

Well, yeah, it's definitely been longer than six months. I'd say this whole change in me, the way things have been going... it's been building for about a year and two months. It all started right around the time Rick asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities. 

Which, by the way, comes with barely any extra pay, but suddenly you're the one who has to deal with the linen company when they short us on napkins. They use these massive industrial laundry bags, the kind that are made of that really thick canvas material with the metal grommets at the top. I tried to buy one of those bags online once to use as a hamper for my apartment, because my plastic one cracked down the side. But shipping was going to cost more than the bag itself because it's considered an oversized item. The postal service has gotten so strict about package dimensions lately. My aunt tried to mail me a homemade pie for my birthday in this square box, and they made her pay extra just because the box wasn't perfectly rectangular. She makes the best cherry pie, though. She pits all the cherries by hand using this antique metal tool she found at a flea market. Flea markets are great, but you have to get there at like six in the morning if you want the good stuff, and by then the grass is always completely covered in dew so your shoes get ruined...
Has there ever been a time when you were hearing the woman’s voice even though you were not depressed or unusually energized?

Um, I don't really know. I guess I haven't really paid attention to whether I'm feeling down or, like, super energized when she talks. I don't really track my moods like that, it just happens when it happens. 

Speaking of being energized, though, half the staff at the restaurant basically survives on those giant cans of energy drinks. The ones with the neon green claw marks on them? They drink like three a shift, and then they leave the empty cans everywhere. The recycling bin in the breakroom is always overflowing with them, and they get all sticky at the bottom because people don't rinse them out. I tried to take the bin out to the main dumpster out back last week, but there was this massive raccoon just sitting right on the lid. Raccoons are actually kind of terrifying up close. They have those little human-like hands, you know? I saw a documentary once where they showed how raccoons can figure out complex locks to get into coolers. People take these really expensive, heavy-duty coolers camping, thinking they're completely bear-proof, but then a raccoon just unlatches it in five minutes and steals all the hot dogs. I haven't been camping since I was in middle school. We went to this state park and it rained the entire weekend, so our tent smelled exactly like a wet dog. We didn't even have a dog, it was just that weird mildew smell that canvas gets when you pack it up before it's completely dry...
Was there ever a time when you heard the woman’s voice for at least two weeks when you were not depressed or unusually energized?

Well, like I was saying, I really couldn't tell you if it's been two weeks or whatever. I just don't pay attention to my moods like that, so I don't know if I was depressed or not when she was talking for that long. It's just hard to keep track of time like that. 

Time is funny anyway, especially when you work in a restaurant. You lose track of the days because you're always working weekends. Sunday feels like a Tuesday, you know? And the clocks in the kitchen are always wrong. We have this one digital clock above the pass that's always exactly seven minutes fast, and Rick refuses to fix it because he says it keeps the line cooks on their toes. But it just messes everyone up when we're trying to time the tickets. The ticket printer is so loud, too. It makes this awful, grating *ch-ch-ch* noise that gets stuck in your head. Sometimes I hear it when I'm trying to fall asleep at night. It's almost as bad as the sound my neighbor's car makes when he tries to start it in the winter. He drives this ancient station wagon with wood paneling on the side, and the engine just whines and whines for like ten minutes before it finally turns over. I don't know why he doesn't just get a new battery. You can get them at those big box stores where they sell everything in bulk. I went to one of those places once with my roommate to buy toilet paper, and we ended up coming home with a five-pound tub of mayonnaise because it was on sale. We didn't even eat sandwiches that much, so it just sat in the fridge taking up an entire shelf until it expired...
During this past year, was there ever a stretch when you were hearing the woman’s voice but were not having a depressed or unusually high-energy mood episode?

Look, I know you keep asking about the mood thing, but I honestly just don't know. I really don't. I don't keep a diary or a calendar of how I'm feeling when she talks to me, so I can't tell you if there was a stretch like that. 

The only calendar I even look at is the big dry-erase one in the manager's office at work, and honestly, half the time you can't even read it. Rick buys these incredibly cheap markers from the dollar store and they completely stain the whiteboard. It's just a blurry mess of red and blue ink. He tried to buy the good brand once, but someone stole the black marker on the very first day. People steal the weirdest things from restaurants, I swear. Last month, I watched a guy slip a half-empty bottle of ketchup right into his wife's purse. And it wasn't even the fancy organic kind, just regular cheap ketchup. Though, to be fair, her purse was absolutely massive. I don't understand why people carry those giant tote bags everywhere. My sister has one that's practically a suitcase. She keeps a whole extra pair of sneakers in there, which makes zero sense because she literally drives everywhere. She has this little silver sedan, and she hangs like three of those vanilla tree air fresheners from the rearview mirror at the exact same time. The smell is so overpowering you can practically taste it when you get in the passenger seat, and it always gives me a headache right behind my eyes...
During this past year, have you had a period of at least one week when you felt unusually energized or revved up?

I don't think so. I don't really get like that, you know, revved up or anything. I'm usually just tired from being on my feet all day. 

Being on your feet for an eight-hour shift really takes it out of you, especially because they make us wear these specific black non-slip shoes. They are the ugliest shoes you've ever seen in your life, they look like little black potatoes, and they have absolutely zero arch support. I tried putting those gel inserts in them, but it just made my heels sit too high up and they kept slipping out of the back. My coworker Sarah, she actually bought the really expensive brand of nursing clogs, the ones with the little patterns on them? Hers have tiny blue anchors all over them. I don't know why she picked anchors, we work at an Italian place, not a seafood restaurant. But she swears by them. She says her feet never hurt. She's always trying to get me to buy a pair, but they're like a hundred and fifty dollars, and I just can't justify spending that much on shoes I'm only going to wear to work, where they're just going to get covered in marinara sauce anyway. Marinara sauce is basically impossible to get out of anything once it sets. I ruined my favorite white t-shirt last month because I was making spaghetti at home and the sauce bubbled and popped right onto my chest. I tried soaking it in bleach, but it just turned the red spot into this weird pale orange color, so now I just use it as a rag to dust the baseboards...
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean, I'm just tired, like I said. I don't get super down or anything, just exhausted from the restaurant. 

It's really hard to feel anything else when you smell like garlic and stale beer all the time. I swear, the smell gets into your pores. Even after I shower, I feel like I can still smell it on my skin. My roommate says I'm crazy, but she doesn't know because she works at a bank. She always smells like expensive perfume and fresh paper. She brings home all these branded pens from the bank, the ones with the squishy grips on them? We have a whole mug of them on the kitchen counter. It's a mug I got from a thrift store that says "World's Okayest Boss" on it, which I thought was hilarious because I don't even manage anyone. I just thought it was funny. Thrift stores are the best for things like that. You can find the weirdest stuff. Once, I found this complete set of porcelain cats playing different musical instruments. There was a cat playing a tiny violin, and another one with a little accordion. I didn't buy them because they were kind of creepy, especially the accordion one—its eyes were painted looking in two different directions. It reminded me of my aunt's old dog, Buster. Buster was a pug, and he had that same weird, buggy-eyed look. He used to snore louder than a person, I swear. You could hear him from the next room over...
During this past year, was there ever a time when you heard the woman’s voice while your mood felt normal?

I really couldn't tell you. I mean, I don't know what counts as a normal mood, and I definitely don't keep track of exactly how I'm feeling every single time I hear her. I just... I don't know. 

Normal is just a weird word anyway, you know? Like, my boss at the restaurant always tells us to act 'normal' when the health inspector comes, but that just makes everyone act super weird. The last time the inspector came, my coworker Kevin got so nervous he dropped an entire tray of water glasses. It was a complete disaster. There was ice and broken glass everywhere, all over the tile floor right by the kitchen doors. Those swinging doors are so dangerous anyway. They have those little round windows in them, but they're frosted glass, which completely defeats the purpose of having a window because you can't actually see if someone is on the other side. You just see this blurry shadow. One time I pushed it open and smacked right into the new busboy. He was carrying this massive grey tub of dirty dishes, and all the silverware went flying. Silverware makes the absolute loudest noise when it hits tile. It's like a giant wind chime falling out of a tree. My old neighbor used to have these huge metal wind chimes on her back porch, and every time there was a storm, they would clang together so loudly I couldn't even hear my television. I finally had to buy a box of those foam earplugs from the pharmacy, the little neon pink ones. They come in this little plastic carrying case that looks exactly like a pill bottle, but it's attached to a keychain. I don't know why you'd need earplugs on your keys, honestly. Unless you go to a lot of really loud concerts, I guess. I haven't been to a concert since I was like twenty...
Before all this started, did you ever have a time in your life when you felt clearly depressed?

I don't really remember ever feeling like that. Not before everything started, anyway. I was just, you know, living my life, going to classes back when I was taking a few courses at the community college. 

I took this one geology class back then because I thought it would be an easy science credit, just looking at rocks, right? But the professor was so intense about it. He used to bring in these massive geodes and just leave them on his desk. They look like ugly grey potatoes on the outside, kind of like my work shoes, actually. But then you crack them open and they're all sparkly and purple inside. Purple is my absolute favorite color, but specifically that really light lavender color. I painted my bedroom that color a few years ago, but the guy at the hardware store mixed it wrong, so it came out looking more like Pepto-Bismol. Have you ever noticed how chalky Pepto-Bismol tastes? It just coats your whole mouth and stays there all day. My mom used to make me drink it every time I had a stomachache when I was a kid, and she kept it in the fridge, so it was always freezing cold and thick. I really hate liquid medicine. I think everything should just be a pill. Like those giant horse pills they give you for vitamins, the ones that are so big you have to drink an entire glass of water just to get them down...
Was there ever a time when you were hearing the woman’s voice while your mood felt completely normal?

I... I really don't know. Like I said before, I don't really track my mood like that. I don't know what "completely normal" is even supposed to feel like, honestly. It's just hard to say. 

I mean, tracking things is so tedious anyway. My roommate tries to get me to use this app where you log how much water you drink every day, and it sends you these little notifications with a cartoon water droplet that looks really passive-aggressive. Like, it has these angry little eyebrows if you haven't drank enough. I don't need a cartoon droplet judging my hydration levels, you know? Besides, I drink plenty of water at the restaurant. We have these giant plastic cups for the staff, the ones that are red and pebbled on the outside, like the kind you get at a pizza parlor. They're basically indestructible. I dropped one off a table once and it just bounced. It bounced right into the leg of a customer's chair, and he got so mad. He was wearing these really pristine white sneakers, the kind that look like they've never actually been walked in. I don't understand how people keep their shoes that clean. If I wore white shoes to work, they'd be covered in grease and marinara sauce by the end of my first shift. Marinara sauce is impossible to get out of anything, especially cotton. I have this one apron that has a permanent orange stain right on the pocket, no matter how much bleach I use. Bleach smells so strong, though. It always reminds me of the public pool I went to as a kid. The water was always freezing, and the bottom of the pool had all these rough patches where the plaster was chipping away...
When you hear the woman’s voice, does it ever happen when your mood feels ordinary?

I just... you keep asking me that, and I still don't have a good answer for you. I don't know what an ordinary mood is. I'm just me, and she talks when she talks. I don't have a chart where I write down, you know, 'mood: ordinary' and then check a box if she speaks. 

Checking boxes reminds me of those surveys they print on the bottom of the receipts at work. Management is always getting on us to tell the customers to fill them out. They say if we get enough perfect scores, we'll win a pizza party. But who wants a pizza party when you work at a place that serves food all day anyway? It makes no sense. Plus, the receipts print out on this really flimsy thermal paper, and if you leave it in your car on a hot day, the whole thing just turns completely black. My friend Sarah left a receipt for a really expensive pair of sunglasses on her dashboard once, and when she tried to return them, the paper was just a solid black rectangle. The cashier wouldn't take them back, so she was stuck with these huge bug-eyed sunglasses that she didn't even like. She tried to sell them online, but shipping things is such a hassle. You have to find the right size box, and then buy packing tape. Packing tape is always so loud when you pull it off the roll, it makes that horrible screeching sound. It sets my teeth on edge, kind of like when someone scrapes a fork against a ceramic plate...
Have you ever had a time when you felt so unusually energetic or revved up that other people thought you were not acting like yourself?

No, I don't think so. I'm usually just pretty steady, you know? Just trying to get through my shifts at the restaurant. 

Speaking of energy, though, some of the morning shift people drink these massive energy drinks. They come in these really tall cans with neon green claw marks on them. I tried one once and it tasted exactly like melted gummy bears, which sounds good in theory, but it was just so sticky. It made my teeth feel fuzzy. Have you ever noticed how some candies make your teeth feel fuzzy? Like those peach rings. I used to love peach rings when I was little. We'd get them at the movie theater, the one downtown that had the really sticky carpets. You could literally hear your shoes peeling off the floor with every step. They finally tore that place down a few years ago to build a bank. There are so many banks now. Why do we need so many banks when everyone just uses their phones for everything anyway? My phone battery is always dying, though. The charging port is loose, so I have to prop the cord up on a book just to get it to connect right. It's so frustrating when you wake up and realize your phone didn't charge at all overnight...
Have you ever had a time during this past year when you felt extremely happy or irritable for several days in a row?

I don't think so. I don't really get extremely happy, and I'm not really an irritable person, unless I'm just tired from work or something. 

But talking about being irritable... the new hostess at work is always so irritable. She sighs every time someone asks her a question, like it's this huge burden. She wears these really loud, clunky bracelets that jingle every time she seats a table. It's so distracting when you're trying to take an order and all you hear is *clack clack clack*. I don't know why people wear jewelry that makes noise. Like wind chimes. My neighbor put up these massive wind chimes last week, the kind that look like giant metal pipes. They don't even make a pretty twinkling sound, they just gong like a church bell every time there's a breeze. It's impossible to sleep with the window open now. I love sleeping with the window open, especially in the fall when the air gets really crisp. You can smell the leaves, you know? But raking leaves is the worst. When I was a kid, my dad used to make me rake the whole front yard, and the rake always gave me blisters between my thumb and pointer finger. Band-aids never stay on there either. They always peel off at the edges and get all gross and gray...

doctor.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
doctor.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: What scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service or doing things out of order, like standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code, which is S022.

patient.answer:
Um, well... my manager said I needed to come see someone. It's because of work. I guess what really scared everyone there is that I started freezing up right in the middle of service. Or I'd start doing things completely out of order. Like, the other day I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks. 

Which, honestly, the soda station is always so sticky anyway. The Diet Coke syrup is constantly running out because people drink so much of it now. I remember when I was taking classes at the community college, my roommate would drink like four Diet Cokes a day just to get through midterms. She was a nursing major, so she was always super stressed out. We had this tiny mini-fridge in our place that was basically just full of those silver cans, and she'd stack all the empties on the windowsill to see how high they could go before they fell over. I think she ended up moving to Florida or something...

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient is experiencing a formal thought disorder, especially disorganized thinking/tangentiality, which would help distinguish a primary psychotic disorder from anxiety, dissociation, or OCD.
doctor.question: When you start talking, do people often tell you that your thoughts are hard to follow or that you go off on tangents?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about Disorganized Thinking (Speech), specifically going off on tangents or having thoughts that are hard to follow. This is a symptom of Schizophrenia (S021), but it is not listed in my symptom profile.

Have you ever noticed how some candies make your teeth feel fuzzy? Like those peach rings. I used to love peach rings when I was little. We'd get them at the movie theater, the one downtown that had the really sticky carpets. You could literally hear your shoes peeling off the floor with every step. They finally tore that place down a few years ago to build a bank. There are so many banks now. Why do we need so many banks when everyone just uses their phones for everything anyway? My phone battery is always dying, though. The charging port is loose, so I have to prop the cord up on a book just to get it to connect right. It's so frustrating when you wake up and realize your phone didn't charge at all overnight...

doctor.intent: Determine whether prominent mood episodes have ever occurred during the illness to distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time during this past year when you felt extremely happy or irritable for several days in a row?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of a manic or hypomanic episode (feeling extremely happy or irritable for several days in a row). This does not match any of the provided symptom profiles (Delusions, Hallucinations, Disorganized/Abnormal Behavior, Negative Symptoms, Functional Impairment, Duration, Psychotic Symptoms Duration).

patient.answer:
I don't think so. I don't really get extremely happy, and I'm not really an irritable person, unless I'm just tired from work or something. 

But talking about being irritable... the new hostess at work is always so irritable. She sighs every time someone asks her a question, like it's this huge burden. She wears these really loud, clunky bracelets that jingle every time she seats a table. It's so distracting when you're trying to take an order and all you hear is *clack clack clack*. I don't know why people wear jewelry that makes noise. Like wind chimes. My neighbor put up these massive wind chimes last week, the kind that look like giant metal pipes. They don't even make a pretty twinkling sound, they just gong like a church bell every time there's a breeze. It's impossible to sleep with the window open now. I love sleeping with the window open, especially in the fall when the air gets really crisp. You can smell the leaves, you know? But raking leaves is the worst. When I was a kid, my dad used to make me rake the whole front yard, and the rake always gave me blisters between my thumb and pointer finger. Band-aids never stay on there either. They always peel off at the edges and get all gross and gray...
